meta.provenance: Authored from model knowledge (cutoff Jan 2026). Original explanations — not copied from Adobe documentation. Shortcuts/menu paths are factual data.
meta.iconNote: Adobe icon artwork is proprietary; app renders software chip fallback.

commands.name: New Project
commands.description: Creates a new project and opens the import view for selecting initial media. Start each film-of-the-project here, and keep one project per film to avoid media chaos.

commands.name: New Sequence
commands.description: Creates a timeline with chosen resolution, frame rate and audio track layout. Easier still: drag a clip onto the New Item button to make a sequence that matches the footage exactly.

commands.name: Sequence Settings
commands.description: Edits the active sequence's frame size, frame rate and preview format after creation. Check it first when renders come out the wrong shape.

commands.name: Import
commands.description: Brings video, image sequences, audio and graphics into the project. Import rendered archviz shots and site footage into clearly named bins from day one.

commands.name: Media Browser
commands.description: Browses drives and card structures with previews, importing media without leaving Premiere. Safer than Explorer for camera cards because it understands their folder formats.

commands.name: New Bin
commands.description: Creates a folder in the Project panel for organising clips. A disciplined bin structure — footage, renders, audio, graphics, sequences — pays off on every project.

commands.name: Create Proxies
commands.description: Generates lightweight copies of heavy footage that Premiere can switch to during editing, then swaps back for export. Essential for cutting 4K renders smoothly on a laptop; toggle them with the monitor's proxy button.

commands.name: Selection Tool
commands.description: Selects, moves and trims clips directly in the timeline. The default tool — return to it after every specialist tool so stray clicks stay harmless.

commands.name: Track Select Forward Tool
commands.description: Selects every clip from the click point to the end of the sequence; Shift+A selects backwards instead. Use it to shove the whole back half of an edit along when inserting a new scene.

commands.name: Ripple Edit Tool
commands.description: Trims a cut and automatically closes the gap, shifting everything downstream. The workhorse trimming tool — tighten shots without ever leaving black holes in the timeline.

commands.name: Rolling Edit Tool
commands.description: Moves the cut point between two clips without changing the overall duration — one clip gets longer, the other shorter. Perfect for retiming a cut to land on a music beat.

commands.name: Rate Stretch Tool
commands.description: Drags a clip's edge to change its playback speed so it fills exactly the space available. Quick for stretching a short flythrough to cover a voiceover line.

commands.name: Razor Tool
commands.description: Cuts a clip into two at the point you click; Shift-click cuts through all tracks. Most editors prefer Add Edit at the playhead, but the razor is direct and visual.

commands.name: Slip Tool
commands.description: Changes which portion of the source footage plays inside a clip without moving the clip or changing its length. Use it to catch the best moment of a camera move while keeping the cut rhythm intact.

commands.name: Slide Tool
commands.description: Moves a clip earlier or later in the sequence while its neighbours trim to absorb the change, keeping total duration fixed. For nudging one shot's position within a locked montage.

commands.name: Pen Tool
commands.description: Adds and adjusts keyframes on timeline rubber bands, such as audio volume and opacity, and draws freeform graphics. Click a clip's volume line with it to keyframe a music dip under narration.

commands.name: Hand Tool
commands.description: Drags the timeline view left and right without moving any clips. Middle-mouse drag does the same from any tool.

commands.name: Zoom Tool
commands.description: Zooms the timeline in where you click, or out with Alt held. Most editors use the plus and minus keys instead, but the tool allows marquee-zooming to an exact region.

commands.name: Mark In
commands.description: Sets the in point on the source monitor or sequence, defining where an edit range begins. The first half of three-point editing — mark the usable part of a shot before cutting it in.

commands.name: Mark Out
commands.description: Sets the out point, completing the range for an insert, overwrite or export. With in and out set on the source, one keystroke drops exactly the shot you chose into the cut.

commands.name: Go to In / Out
commands.menu: Markers > Go to In Point / Go to Out Point
commands.description: Jumps the playhead straight to the marked in or out point. Keeps three-point editing entirely on the keyboard.

commands.name: Clear In and Out
commands.description: Removes the current in and out points in one stroke. Clear stale ranges before exporting, or you may accidentally export only a fragment.

commands.name: Insert
commands.description: Places the source clip at the playhead and pushes existing material later to make room. Use it when adding a shot mid-sequence without overwriting anything.

commands.name: Overwrite
commands.description: Places the source clip at the playhead on top of whatever is there, without shifting the sequence. The standard edit when laying shots over a locked music bed.

commands.name: Lift
commands.description: Removes the material between the sequence in and out points, leaving a gap. Use it when timing elsewhere must not move.

commands.name: Extract
commands.description: Removes the material between in and out and ripples the gap closed. The range-based sibling of ripple delete, ideal for cutting a flabby section out of a draft.

commands.name: Add Edit
commands.description: Cuts the clips on targeted tracks at the playhead — a keyboard razor. Add Ctrl+Shift+K to cut through every track at once.

commands.name: Ripple Delete
commands.menu: Right-click clip or gap > Ripple Delete
commands.description: Deletes a clip or gap and closes the hole by pulling everything after it forward. The fastest way to keep a rough cut gapless as you strip out weak shots.

commands.name: Snap
commands.description: Toggles magnetic snapping of clip edges to other edits, markers and the playhead. Leave it on for assembly; flick it off for delicate frame-level nudges.

commands.name: Add Marker
commands.description: Drops a marker on the clip or sequence at the playhead, with optional notes and colours. Tap it on every music beat first, then cut shots to the markers.

commands.name: Go to Next Marker
commands.description: Jumps the playhead to the next marker; Ctrl+Shift+M goes back to the previous one. Turns beat markers into a navigation system for the whole edit.

commands.name: Match Frame
commands.description: Loads the source clip into the Source Monitor parked on the exact frame under the playhead. Use it to grab an alternative take or extend a shot from its original footage.

commands.name: Select Clip at Playhead
commands.description: Selects whatever clip sits under the playhead on targeted tracks. Combined with property shortcuts it enables rapid keyboard-only clip adjustments.

commands.name: Ripple Trim Previous Edit
commands.menu: Sequence > Ripple Trim Previous Edit Point to Playhead
commands.description: Trims from the previous cut up to the playhead and ripples the sequence closed. Park the playhead where the shot should start and tap Q — brutal, fast top-trimming.

commands.name: Ripple Trim Next Edit
commands.menu: Sequence > Ripple Trim Next Edit Point to Playhead
commands.description: Trims from the playhead forward to the next cut and closes the gap. The tail-trimming twin of Q — together they make rough cuts astonishingly quick.

commands.name: Extend Selected Edit
commands.menu: Sequence > Extend Selected Edit to Playhead
commands.description: Rolls the selected edit point to the playhead position, lengthening one clip and shortening its neighbour. Select a cut, park the playhead on the beat, press E.

commands.name: Toggle Trim Type
commands.menu: Double-click an edit point to enter trim mode; Shift+T cycles trim type
commands.description: Cycles the selected edit point between regular, ripple and rolling trims, shown by red or yellow brackets. Double-clicking a cut opens the dedicated trim view for refining it while looping playback.

commands.name: Speed/Duration
commands.description: Sets a clip's playback speed by percentage or target duration, with reverse and frame-blending options. Slow a 50 fps site clip to 50 percent for smooth half-speed motion.

commands.name: Time Remapping
commands.menu: Clip > Show Clip Keyframes > Time Remapping > Speed
commands.description: Keyframes a clip's speed over time directly on the timeline rubber band, allowing ramps between fast and slow. Use it to glide quickly through a corridor then linger in the main space.

commands.name: Nest
commands.description: Collapses selected clips into a single nested sequence that can be trimmed and effected as one. Nest a finished montage section before applying a unified grade or transition.

commands.name: Group
commands.description: Links selected clips so they select and move together, without creating a new sequence. Lighter-weight than nesting for keeping a title and its backing plate in sync.

commands.name: Ungroup
commands.description: Releases grouped clips back to independent selection. Necessary before trimming one member differently from the rest.

commands.name: Link / Unlink
commands.description: Joins or separates a clip's video and audio so they move together or independently. Unlink to delete scratch audio from renders, or to slip sound against picture for a J-cut.

commands.name: Enable Clip
commands.description: Toggles a clip on or off without deleting it — disabled clips render black and silent. Useful for comparing versions of a shot or muting an overlay during review.

commands.name: Label Colours
commands.description: Assigns colours to clips in the project and timeline. Colour-code by content — renders, drone footage, graphics, audio — so the timeline reads at a glance.

commands.name: Replace with Clip
commands.menu: Right-click timeline clip > Replace With Clip > From Source Monitor
commands.description: Swaps a timeline clip for the Source Monitor clip while keeping its position, duration and applied effects. Ideal for dropping in an updated render over an old placeholder version.

commands.name: Synchronise Clips
commands.description: Aligns selected clips by their audio waveforms or timecode. The rescue for interview or walkthrough footage where camera audio and a separate recorder must line up.

commands.name: Merge Clips
commands.description: Combines a video clip with separately recorded audio into a single new clip for editing. Merge once in the project so every future cut uses the good sound automatically.

commands.name: Paste Attributes
commands.description: Pastes chosen properties — motion, opacity, effects, colour — from a copied clip onto others. Grade one shot, then paste its Lumetri settings across the whole scene.

commands.name: Audio Gain
commands.description: Adjusts a clip's audio level before it reaches the mixer, with a normalise option to a target loudness. Set music and voiceover gains here first, then fine-tune with keyframes.

commands.name: Audio Track Mixer
commands.description: A mixing-desk view with faders, pans and effects per track rather than per clip. Balance the music, ambience and narration tracks of a film here as a whole.

commands.name: Essential Sound Panel
commands.description: Tags audio as dialogue, music, SFX or ambience and offers plain-language tools — loudness matching, ducking, repair. Auto-ducking music under a voiceover takes seconds here.

commands.name: Mute / Solo Track
commands.menu: Timeline track header M and S buttons
commands.description: Silences a track (M) or isolates it (S) during playback. Solo the narration to check clarity, mute the music to hear what the ambience is really doing.

commands.name: Show Audio Waveforms
commands.menu: Timeline wrench menu > Show Audio Waveform
commands.description: Displays waveforms on audio clips in the timeline. Expand the music track's height and cut visually to the drum hits.

commands.name: Effect Controls Panel
commands.description: Edits the selected clip's built-in motion, opacity and speed properties plus any applied effects, with keyframing. Where you scale a render to punch in, or keyframe a slow push on a still.

commands.name: Effects Panel
commands.description: Searches all video and audio effects and transitions for dragging onto clips. Type-search it rather than browsing — the folder tree is deep.

commands.name: Apply Video Transition
commands.description: Adds the default transition — normally a cross dissolve — to the selected edit points. Set your preferred duration in preferences, and resist using anything fancier without a reason.

commands.name: Apply Audio Transition
commands.description: Adds the default constant-power crossfade to selected audio edits. A short crossfade on every music and ambience cut removes clicks and bumps instantly.

commands.name: Lumetri Colour Panel
commands.description: The main grading interface — basic correction, creative LUTs, curves, colour wheels, HSL secondaries and vignette. Grade shot-matched sections on adjustment layers to keep the film's look coherent.

commands.name: Lumetri Scopes
commands.description: Displays waveform, vectorscope and histogram readouts of the programme image. Trust the scopes over your monitor when checking exposure and skin tones for delivery.

commands.name: Adjustment Layer
commands.description: Creates a transparent layer whose effects apply to every track beneath it. Lay one across a scene and grade it once instead of clip by clip.

commands.name: Warp Stabiliser
commands.menu: Effects > Video Effects > Distort > Warp Stabilizer
commands.description: Analyses and smooths shaky footage directly in the timeline. Apply it to handheld site walkthroughs; use Smooth Motion rather than No Motion to keep some life in the shot.

commands.name: Masking and Tracking
commands.menu: Effect Controls > effect mask (ellipse, rectangle, pen) + tracker
commands.description: Draws a mask on any effect so it applies only inside the shape, then tracks the mask to follow movement through the shot. Use it to brighten just the building facade or blur a passer-by's face.

commands.name: Essential Graphics Panel
commands.description: Builds and edits titles, shapes and layered graphics, and browses installed Motion Graphics templates. Design a consistent lower-third for project captions once and reuse it throughout.

commands.name: Type Tool
commands.description: Creates text directly in the Programme Monitor as a graphic clip on the timeline. Fine for quick captions; style the result properly in the Essential Graphics panel.

commands.name: Install Motion Graphics Template
commands.menu: Graphics and Titles > Install Motion Graphics Template (.mogrt)
commands.description: Adds a .mogrt file — often built in After Effects — to the Essential Graphics library for drag-and-drop use. Package your studio's animated titles as MOGRTs so every film shares the same identity.

commands.name: Export
commands.description: Opens the export view for choosing format, preset, range and destination. H.264 with a high-bitrate preset covers most client review and web delivery needs.

commands.name: Export In to Out Range
commands.description: Exports only the section between the sequence in and out points. Perfect for sending a single revised scene rather than re-rendering the whole film.

commands.name: Send to Media Encoder Queue
commands.menu: Export view > Send to Media Encoder
commands.description: Queues the export in Adobe Media Encoder so rendering happens in the background. Stack multiple formats — a 4K master and a compressed review copy — and keep editing meanwhile.

commands.name: Render In to Out
commands.description: Pre-renders the effects-heavy sections of the marked range so the timeline plays back smoothly, turning the render bar green. Do it before client playback sessions to avoid stutters.

commands.name: Play/Stop
commands.description: Starts and stops playback in the active monitor. The most-pressed key in editing; pair it with JKL for speed control.

commands.name: JKL Playback
commands.description: Shuttle controls: L plays forward and speeds up on repeat presses, J does the same in reverse, K pauses. The professional way to scrub footage while logging site material.

commands.name: Play Around
commands.description: Plays a few seconds either side of the playhead and stops. The quickest way to judge a trim in context without manually rewinding.

commands.name: Step One Frame
commands.description: Nudges the playhead a single frame backwards or forwards; Shift+arrow jumps five frames. Frame-stepping is how you find the exact cut point on a beat.

commands.name: Go to Next Edit Point
commands.description: Jumps the playhead to the next or previous cut on targeted tracks. Combined with Q, W and E it makes trimming an entirely keyboard-driven rhythm.

commands.name: Toggle Full Screen
commands.menu: Ctrl+` toggles full-screen playback of the active monitor
commands.description: Expands the active monitor to fill the screen for distraction-free review. Use it when showing a work-in-progress cut to colleagues at your desk.

commands.name: Maximise Frame
commands.menu: Press ` with the pointer over a panel
commands.description: Temporarily expands the panel under the cursor to fill the workspace; press again to restore. Maximise the timeline for complex multi-track passages, then pop back.

commands.name: Zoom Timeline In / Out
commands.description: Zooms the timeline view in and out around the playhead. Zoom in for frame-accurate trims, out for judging overall pacing.

commands.name: Zoom to Sequence
commands.description: Fits the entire sequence into the timeline window. Tap it whenever you are lost deep in a zoomed view.

commands.name: Project Panel
commands.description: Focuses the Project panel, home of all bins, clips and sequences. Keyboard panel-switching (Shift+1 to Shift+9) keeps hands off the mouse during assembly.

commands.name: Source Monitor
commands.description: Focuses the Source Monitor, where raw clips are reviewed and marked before editing into the sequence. Load, mark in and out, then insert or overwrite — the classic loop.

commands.name: Timeline Panel
commands.description: Focuses the timeline, where the film is actually built. Panel focus matters — many shortcuts act on whichever panel is active.

commands.name: Programme Monitor
commands.description: Focuses the Programme Monitor, showing the sequence at the playhead. Its safe margins, playback resolution and comparison view all live in its settings menu.

commands.name: Deselect All
commands.description: Clears the current selection in the active panel. Worth internalising because several commands behave differently when clips are selected versus not.
